text:
Marco: Heads up — SRE flagged a lot of noisy cross-project quota alerts. They suggested adding project-bound API keys so quotas and telemetry are attributed at project-level instead of org-level. Thoughts?

Sasha: +1 from infra. We keep getting org-wide spikes and it's hard to tell which product caused it. Project keys would make quota graphs meaningful. :+1:

Leah: Concern: UX and key explosion. Do we plan per-service account keys or let users mint unlimited project keys? Need console limits and naming.

Tomas: We should also think routing: if a request comes with a project-scoped key but the model instance lives in org pool, do we route differently? Maybe enforce token->project mapping in the router and apply project quota at ingress.

Nina: Implementation thought: add `X-Redwood-Project` claim embedded in key, verify in authn middleware. Example token header: `Authorization: Bearer proj_abc123...` and service validates project id then applies quota/telemetry tags.

Marco: +1 on middleware validation. Also want to make telemetry exportable: include `project_id` and `service_account_id` tags in traces and metrics so billing and latency dashboards can slice by project.

Sasha: Telemetry detail: we need stable keys for attribution in long-running cached responses. If we allow key rotation, include `kid` header and keep a mapping table in auth service. Otherwise caching will lose attribution.

Leah: UX debate: Should console show a single "org key" page and a separate "project keys" tab? We could let org admins toggle project-key enforcement (opt-in) per org, to avoid sudden breakage.

Tomas: Rollout plan proposal: opt-in beta for 10% of orgs, then 50%, then org-wide mandatory after 3 months. Beta traffic will route through new auth path that attaches `project_id` telemetry tag. We'll keep fallback to org-level behavior when `project_id` missing.

Nina: Quota model: evaluate whether to keep quotas hierarchical (org cap + per-project soft quotas) or move to strict per-project ceilings. My preference: org cap + project soft quotas with alerting, then let admins convert soft->hard.

Leah: Agreed. Soft quotas reduce surprise. Also need console affordances: bulk key creation, labels, and revoke. Add "service account delegation" flow to let apps mint short-lived project-bound keys.

Marco: Security note: service accounts should be able to mint scoped keys only if they have a `projects:mint_key` grant. Add audit events for mint/rotate/revoke.

Sasha: From infra perspective, router needs a fast map from key -> (org,project,quota tier). We can cache in router with TTL and listen to changes via pubsub. Key revokes must invalidate quickly.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: authn-middleware v2 -> staging at 1923456799, router cache changes -> staging at 1923456803

Tomas: Action items: 1) auth team to add `project_id` claim + KID support (Nina) 2) infra to prototype router cache invalidation and tag propagation (Sasha) 3) console to design project-key UX + admin toggles (Leah) 4) SRE to define soft quota thresholds and alerting (Marco).

Nina: I'll open a RFC with schema for token claims + telemetry keys and include sample curl for minting:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/projects/abc/keys -H "Authorization: Bearer sa_jkl..." -d '{"name":"ml-ingest","scopes":["generate","embed"]}'
```

Leah: I'll mock console screens this afternoon and drop them in #design.

Marco: Cool. Let's not forget backwards compatibility docs and a migration guide for orgs that want to split traffic into projects. Thanks everyone.
